findings.title: Nil TopicUser causes 500 on unsubscribe
findings.body: `TopicUser.find_by` returns nil when the user has no topic_users row, for example a user notified through a mention or a category watch who never visited the topic. The next line calls `tu.notification_level` on nil and raises NoMethodError. Create the record if it is missing, or use `TopicUser.change`.

findings.title: Repeated GET toggles state and mutates on GET
findings.body: The unsubscribe action changes state on a GET request. A user whose level is already regular gets set to muted. Every revisit of the link, a link prefetch, or an email scanner fetching the URL lowers the level further or changes it unexpectedly. A state-changing GET is also CSRF-able: any third-party page can embed the URL and change a logged-in user's notification level.

findings.title: Direct save bypasses TopicUser.change side effects
findings.body: `tu.save!` skips what `TopicUser.change` normally does. It does not set `notifications_reason_id` or `notifications_changed_at`, and it does not publish the MessageBus notification_level_change. As a result, open clients do not update, and later auto-tracking can override the user's explicit choice because the reason stays nil.

findings.title: No visibility check before modifying TopicUser
findings.body: `TopicView.new` in the unsubscribe action is called without the slug-redirect handling used in `show`. The action then creates or modifies state for the topic, so the guard enforced by TopicView is the only protection. There is also no handling for a missing topic: `@topic_view.topic.unsubscribe_url` is used when the slug is blank.

findings.title: Added explicit render :show may double-render
findings.body: This change adds `render :show` inside `format.html` in `perform_show_response`. `show` then calls `canonical_url` after `perform_show_response`. Other callers may already rely on implicit rendering, so the change risks a DoubleRenderError. It also alters existing `show` behavior even though only `unsubscribe` needed it.

findings.title: Client route fetches normal topic view, not unsubscribe endpoint
findings.body: The client route loads the topic through `PostStream.loadTopicView`, which calls the normal topic JSON endpoint and never hits `/unsubscribe`. When a user navigates to this route inside the app, no unsubscribe happens, yet the page still says "You will stop receiving notifications".

findings.title: No tests for the unsubscribe controller action
findings.body: The new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action has no specs. Untested paths include the regular-to-muted transition, the redirect when the slug does not match, and the case where no TopicUser row exists, which currently crashes.
